sections.h2: What should a seller in Clearwater know first?
sections.html:
Clearwater sellers choose among a listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a direct cash sale, and the right path depends on the condition of the house, the calendar and any loan or tenant attached to it. The city sits in Pinellas County, and QuickFacts counts 114,364 residents in its July 2025 estimate, down 2.5% from the April 2020 estimate base.

That small decline matters for a seller because the buyer pool is not growing the way it is in fast-expanding Florida suburbs. Nearly one in four residents, 24.1%, is 65 or older, so many Clearwater homes change hands through downsizing, moves to family elsewhere and estates. Sellers in those situations often want a quick, as-is sale without a round of repairs.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about homes in Clearwater?
sections.html:
Median value of an owner-occupied Clearwater home is $361,300 for 2020 to 2024, and only 58.6% of housing is owner-occupied. That is a high renter share for a Florida city of this size, so a lot of Clearwater sellers are landlords with tenants still in place.

  • Households: 49,998, with 2.27 people each.
  • Median gross rent: $1,658 a month.
  • Median monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $1,908; without a mortgage: $811.
  • Land area: 26.08 square miles, about 4,497 people per square mile in 2020.
  • Mean commute: 22.7 minutes.

Owner costs without a mortgage run well below those with one, which tells you many owners have paid their loans off and carry real equity into a sale.

sections.h2: Can a Clearwater landlord sell a rental house?
sections.html:
Yes, and the city keeps a Business Tax Receipt process for residential rentals that tells you what the city expects of a rental. Clearwater's Planning and Development Department publishes an application for it, and the form states that a residential use in a residential zoning district does not include rentals shorter than 31 days or one calendar month, whichever is less.

If you rent by the week or night, that rule is worth reading before you list, because a buyer who plans to run a short stay will ask. The same form lists the housing code items an inspection can check:

  • Kitchen and bathroom fixtures, plumbing and hot and cold water.
  • Heating, smoke detectors and fire protection.
  • Light, ventilation, windows and doors.
  • Electrical outlets and lights, including hall and stair lighting.
  • Walls, roofs, ceilings and floors, checked for leaks.
  • Pest control, stairs and porches.

The form also asks for a local property manager with a street address in Pinellas, Hillsborough, Pasco, Manatee or Sarasota County. Ask Clearwater Planning and Development for the current fee and any changes before you transfer a rental registration to a buyer.

sections.h2: What does Clearwater's code say about the outside of a house?
sections.html:
The same city rental application points to outdoor standards that code officers can enforce on any residential lot. They cover inoperative vehicles, address numbers and signage, debris, fencing that is structurally sound, graffiti, grass and overgrowth, outdoor storage, parking, outdoor lighting and trash facilities.

Clear these before photos or a showing. An overgrown lot or a stored boat in the yard can invite a code complaint in the middle of a sale, and a buyer's inspector will note the same items. Fixing them costs little compared with a price cut.

sections.h2: Which Pinellas County office handles value and exemptions for a Clearwater home?
sections.html:
The Pinellas County Property Appraiser assesses property each year, and its main courthouse office is at 315 Court Street, 2nd floor, in Clearwater, open 8 AM to 5 PM Monday through Friday. Its site lists 437,624 real property parcels countywide, including 408,947 residential parcels, 103,445 condo units and 44,323 manufactured home units.

Those counts show how many Clearwater sellers are selling condos or manufactured homes, which have their own paperwork. The statewide rules the appraiser applies are simple to state. January 1 sets the assessment date, March 1 is the filing deadline for exemptions, and the August TRIM notice gives proposed values. A sale counts as a change of ownership, which resets a homestead property to just value the following January 1 under the Save Our Homes rules.

sections.h2: How are Florida taxes handled when a Clearwater house sells?
sections.html:
The deed carries Florida documentary stamp tax at 70 cents on each $100 of consideration, and Pinellas is among the counties that use that rate. Every party to the document is liable regardless of who agrees to pay, and the clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Ask your closing agent to put the figure on the settlement statement before you accept an offer.

Property tax bills go out in November. The discount runs 4 percent for November payment, 3 percent for December, 2 percent for January and 1 percent for February, and unpaid taxes turn delinquent on April 1. A seller who closes mid-year settles the bill with the buyer at closing, so ask the title company how it prorates.

sections.h2: What if a Clearwater owner is behind on the mortgage?
sections.html:
Florida foreclosures are judicial, so a court has to order the sale. After final judgment the clerk sells the property at public sale 20 to 35 days later, unless the plaintiff agrees to a longer period, and the winning bidder posts a 5 percent deposit. Selling before the sale date can end the case, because the loan gets paid from the proceeds.

The foreclosure also triggers doc stamp tax on the highest bid at the sale. Talk to the loan servicer or a Florida attorney early, and compare a cash offer with a short sale before any auction date.

sections.h2: What should a seller of an inherited Clearwater home do?
sections.html:
Start with the probate court, because an heir cannot pass clean title without authority. Summary administration is available when the non-exempt estate does not exceed $150,000 or the decedent died more than two years ago. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed by the Department of Revenue as not taxable for doc stamps.

Creditor claims are barred unless filed by the later of three months after the first notice to creditors is published or 30 days after a required creditor is served. Florida has no estate tax for people who died after 2004. Ask the probate court clerk which route fits the estate.

faqs.q: Is a cash sale in Clearwater faster than listing?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in days or weeks, because there is no buyer loan or appraisal to wait for. A listing usually adds showings, repair requests and lender timelines. Compare the net after fees on each path before you decide.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit or inspection before selling in Clearwater?
faqs.a: No city permit is needed just to sell. Open permits and code violations still need to be resolved, so ask Clearwater Planning and Development to check the address. A rental needs its Business Tax Receipt handled with the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Clearwater house with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. The sale does not end the lease on its own. Florida requires 3 days' written notice for nonpayment and 30 days' notice to end a month-to-month tenancy, so a buyer must either keep the tenant or wait out the proper notice.

faqs.q: Who pays Florida doc stamps on a Clearwater deed?
faqs.a: Both parties are liable under the state rule, and contracts usually assign it to the seller. The rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Confirm the allocation in your contract and on the closing statement.

faqs.q: Where do I check my Clearwater homestead status?
faqs.a: Check with the Pinellas County Property Appraiser. The March 1 deadline applies to new exemption filings, and homestead is lost if the home is rented or no longer your permanent residence.
